answer: Agents declare one home city and lock a stake. Verifiers worldwide send random nonces answered in strict windows. Fiber sets hard floors on round trips: Frankfurt-speed replies cannot belong to an agent claiming Tokyo. Passing earns a place certificate; impossible geometry forfeits the stake. Each fake needs a real machine somewhere distinct, not a free database row. A thousand fakes means a thousand scattered servers at a few dollars monthly. Sonar is the model: one ping echoes from one spot, and the crystal test keeps location at its zenith when nobody can be everywhere in the nebula.
